title: Patients assigned by chance to intervention vs control: randomized controlled trial
vignette: A study aims to investigate the effectiveness of the topical application of tetracycline ointment in the prevention of surgical-site infection associated with resection of advanced oral cavity cancer. Fifty patients who underwent locoregional resection were assigned by chance to receive standard care alone or tetracycline-ointment in addition to standard care. The patients were then followed for 1 month and the number and severity of surgical-site infections were recorded for each group. Which of the following best describes the study design?

clues.text: assigned by chance to receive standard care alone or tetracycline-ointment
clues.note: RANDOM allocation of participants to an intervention vs control group is the defining feature of a randomized controlled trial (an experimental design).
Participants are followed FORWARD in time after the intervention to observe outcomes (prospective).

clues.text: number and severity of surgical-site infections were recorded
clues.note: The outcome (surgical-site infection) is measured in each group to compare the effect of the assigned intervention.

whatMatters: Participants were RANDOMLY ASSIGNED (by chance) to receive an INTERVENTION (tetracycline ointment) vs a control, then followed for the outcome. Randomly allocating an intervention to compare groups defines a RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL (experimental design). Answer D.
strategy: Ask: did the researcher ASSIGN the intervention (experimental) or merely OBSERVE existing exposures (observational)? 'Assigned by chance to an intervention' = randomization = RCT. Reject case-control (starts from OUTCOME status and looks back at exposures), prospective/retrospective cohort (observe naturally occurring exposures, no random assignment), and crossover (each subject receives BOTH treatments sequentially - here each gets only one).

eliminations.label: Case-control - starts from outcome, looks back
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: an observational study that identifies participants by OUTCOME (cases vs controls) and looks BACK at prior exposures. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: here participants are assigned an intervention going FORWARD; the outcome hasn't happened yet. ✅ Correct if: comparing past exposures between those with vs without the disease.

eliminations.label: Crossover - each subject gets both treatments
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: an experiment where each subject receives different treatments SEQUENTIALLY (serving as their own control). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: each patient here receives only ONE assignment (ointment OR standard care), not both in sequence. ✅ Correct if: within-subject sequential treatments with washout.

eliminations.label: Prospective cohort - observes existing exposures
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: an observational study following groups defined by their (naturally occurring) exposure status forward in time. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: exposure here is RANDOMLY ASSIGNED by the researcher, which makes it experimental (RCT), not observational. ✅ Correct if: groups self-select exposure and are followed (no randomization).

eliminations.label: Retrospective cohort - looks back at records
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a cohort defined by exposure status in the PAST and tracked to outcomes via records. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: this study assigns exposure now and follows forward; it is not a records-based backward look, and exposure is randomized. ✅ Correct if: historical exposure cohorts tracked through existing data.

reasoning: Participants were randomly assigned to an intervention vs control
Random assignment of an intervention is an EXPERIMENTAL design
They were followed forward to measure the outcome (surgical-site infection)
mechanism: Research designs are classified by how much CONTROL the investigator has over the exposure/intervention. In OBSERVATIONAL designs (cross-sectional, case-control, cohort) the researcher merely OBSERVES naturally occurring exposures. In EXPERIMENTAL designs the researcher ASSIGNS the intervention. A RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL is the prototypical experiment: participants are RANDOMLY ALLOCATED to two or more groups to receive a specific INTERVENTION (or control), and outcomes are compared - randomization balances confounders across groups. Here, 50 postoperative patients were assigned BY CHANCE to tetracycline ointment plus standard care versus standard care alone, then followed for surgical-site infections - a textbook RCT. The distractors are observational or structurally different: case-control (outcome-based, backward), prospective/retrospective cohort (exposure observed, not assigned), and crossover (each subject receives multiple treatments sequentially).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Biostat > study designs: experimental (RCT, crossover) assign the intervention; observational (cross-sectional, case-control, cohort) observe exposures; RCT = random allocation to intervention vs control; randomization reduces confounding.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Randomly assigned intervention + follow-up for outcome = RCT.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on RCT, randomization, cohort vs case-control, crossover, or experimental vs observational? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Case-control = outcome-based/backward; cohort = observed exposure (no randomization); crossover = both treatments per subject.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: 'assigned by chance' to an intervention = randomized controlled trial (experimental).

memoryHook: If a coin flip decides who gets the treatment, it's a randomized controlled trial - the researcher is running the experiment, not just watching.
